items.title: A client with suspected DVT should not have the affected leg ___. The nurse should assess for pulmonary embolism symptoms such as sudden ___ and chest pain.
items.content: massaged|dyspnea
items.rationale: Massage is avoided because of embolization concern. Sudden dyspnea and chest pain may indicate PE and require emergency evaluation.

items.title: A client is found unresponsive with RR 5/min, pinpoint pupils, and suspected opioid exposure. Select the condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:opioid overdose with respiratory depression|actions:provide airway and ventilatory support;administer naloxone and repeat per protocol if needed|monitor:respiratory rate and oxygenation;level of consciousness and recurrent sedation
items.rationale: Ventilation is the immediate priority. Naloxone reverses opioid effects but may wear off before the opioid, so monitor for recurrence.

items.title: Highlight findings suggesting acute kidney injury: rising creatinine;reduced urine output;new hyperkalemia;stable baseline creatinine;new fluid overload.
items.content: segments:rising creatinine|reduced urine output|new hyperkalemia|stable baseline creatinine|new fluid overload|correct:1,2,3,5
items.rationale: Rising creatinine, oliguria, hyperkalemia, and fluid overload are complications or indicators of acute kidney injury.

items.title: A client is prescribed 1.2 g of an antibiotic. The vial concentration after reconstitution is 400 mg/mL. How many mL are needed?
A client's lactate decreases from 5.2 to 4.7 to 4.5 mmol/L after initial treatment but remains elevated. What is the best interpretation?
items.content: Perfusion may be improving slowly but remains abnormal; continue reassessment and prescribed sepsis management.
items.rationale: A downward trend is encouraging, but persistent elevation may indicate ongoing hypoperfusion or other causes and needs continued evaluation.

items.title: A client with a tibial fracture in a cast reports escalating pain despite medication. The calf is tense, pain increases with passive stretch, and sensation is tingling. What should the nurse do?
items.content: Notify the orthopedic surgeon immediately, perform and document neurovascular checks, keep the limb at heart level, and prepare for urgent cast release or fasciotomy as directed.
items.rationale: Pain out of proportion, passive-stretch pain, tense swelling, and paresthesia suggest compartment syndrome. Delay can cause irreversible muscle and nerve injury.

items.title: A client with pneumonia is confused, febrile, and hypotensive. BP is 82/46 mm Hg, lactate is 4.3 mmol/L, and oxygen saturation is 91%. Which action should the nurse prioritize while the sepsis response is activated?
items.content: Establish large-bore IV access and begin the prescribed isotonic crystalloid bolus, reassessing perfusion frequently.
items.rationale: Hypotension with elevated lactate indicates impaired tissue perfusion. Prompt isotonic fluid resuscitation is a priority unless contraindicated; reassess response and prepare for vasopressors if hypotension persists.

items.title: A conscious client with diabetes reports tremors and diaphoresis. Capillary glucose is 54 mg/dL. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.content: Give 15 g of rapid-acting oral carbohydrate; recheck glucose in 15 minutes; repeat treatment if glucose remains below 70 mg/dL; provide a snack or meal when glucose recovers if the next meal is not imminent.
items.rationale: A conscious client who can swallow safely should receive rapid carbohydrate, followed by a 15-minute recheck and repeat treatment if needed. Severe altered consciousness or inability to swallow requires glucagon or IV dextrose rather than oral intake.

items.title: A client receiving magnesium sulfate for severe preeclampsia has a respiratory rate of 10/min, absent patellar reflexes, and urine output of 20 mL/hr. Identify the three immediate nursing actions.
items.content: Stop the magnesium sulfate infusion; notify the provider and activate urgent clinical response; prepare to administer prescribed calcium gluconate.
items.rationale: Respiratory depression, loss of reflexes, and oliguria suggest magnesium toxicity and reduced clearance. Stop the infusion, escalate immediately, support breathing, and prepare the antidote.

items.title: For each condition, identify the most appropriate additional precaution.
items.content: Pulmonary tuberculosis — Airborne; Clostridioides difficile infection — Contact; Influenza — Droplet; Disseminated herpes zoster — Airborne and Contact.
items.rationale: Precautions are selected by transmission route. C. difficile requires soap-and-water hand hygiene because spores resist alcohol-based sanitizer; disseminated zoster requires airborne and contact precautions.

items.title: Fifteen minutes after a packed RBC transfusion begins, the client develops chills, flank pain, and fever. The nurse should first ___ the transfusion and then maintain IV access with ___ using new tubing.
items.content: stop|normal saline
items.rationale: Stop the transfusion immediately for a suspected acute reaction. Keep the vein open with normal saline through new tubing, assess the client, notify the provider and blood bank, and follow facility protocol.

items.title: A client develops facial droop, dysarthria, and left-sided weakness 40 minutes ago. Glucose is 112 mg/dL and BP is 178/96 mm Hg. Complete the bowtie: identify the likely condition, two priority actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:acute stroke, likely ischemic|actions:activate stroke response and establish last-known-well time; arrange urgent noncontrast head CT and keep the client NPO until swallow screening|monitor:neurologic status using a standardized stroke scale; blood pressure and oxygenation
items.rationale: Time-sensitive stroke evaluation requires rapid activation, accurate last-known-well time, and urgent imaging to distinguish ischemia from hemorrhage. Avoid oral intake until swallowing is assessed to reduce aspiration risk.

items.title: Review the assessment note and identify the findings that indicate severe dehydration requiring urgent escalation.
items.content: An 8-month-old has had vomiting and diarrhea for 2 days. The infant is lethargic, has sunken eyes, a very dry mouth, capillary refill of 5 seconds, weak peripheral pulses, and no wet diaper for 10 hours. Temperature is 37.8°C.
items.rationale: Lethargy, markedly delayed capillary refill, weak pulses, and prolonged absence of urine indicate poor perfusion and severe fluid deficit. Sunken eyes and dry mucosa support dehydration.

items.title: The prescription is heparin 18 units/kg/hr for a client weighing 72 kg. The IV bag contains 25,000 units in 500 mL. How many mL/hr should the nurse program? Round to the nearest tenth.
items.content: 25.9 mL/hr
items.rationale: 18 units/kg/hr × 72 kg = 1,296 units/hr. The concentration is 25,000 units ÷ 500 mL = 50 units/mL. 1,296 ÷ 50 = 25.92 mL/hr, rounded to 25.9 mL/hr. Verify the calculation and infusion with the required independent double-check policy.

items.title: A client admitted with pneumonia has the following trend: 0800 RR 22/min, SpO₂ 94% on 2 L/min, alert; 1000 RR 30/min, SpO₂ 90% on 4 L/min, restless; 1200 RR 34/min, SpO₂ 86% on 6 L/min, drowsy. What is the priority interpretation and response?
items.content: The client is deteriorating with worsening hypoxemic respiratory failure; call rapid response/emergency support and prepare for advanced airway and ventilatory support.
items.rationale: Increasing oxygen requirement with falling saturation, tachypnea, and declining mental status indicates progressive respiratory failure. Escalate immediately rather than simply increasing oxygen without reassessment.

items.title: A 19-year-old with type 1 diabetes presents with vomiting, abdominal pain, deep rapid respirations, and fruity breath. Glucose is 486 mg/dL, pH 7.18, bicarbonate 10 mEq/L, potassium 5.4 mEq/L, and serum ketones are positive. Which initial intervention is the priority?
items.content: Begin prescribed isotonic IV fluid replacement and initiate close cardiac and electrolyte monitoring while preparing for IV insulin after potassium is assessed.
items.rationale: DKA causes profound dehydration and acidosis. Initial isotonic fluid resuscitation is essential. Serum potassium may be elevated despite total-body depletion; insulin shifts potassium intracellularly, so potassium must be monitored and managed safely.

items.title: On postoperative day 2 after hip replacement, a client suddenly develops dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, HR 132/min, and SpO₂ 84%. Which nursing actions should be taken immediately? Select all that apply.
items.content: Activate rapid response/emergency support; apply oxygen and support ventilation; keep the client on bed rest and avoid ambulation; maintain IV access and prepare for diagnostic evaluation and prescribed anticoagulation; continuously monitor oxygenation and hemodynamic status.
items.rationale: Sudden hypoxemia, tachycardia, and pleuritic pain after orthopedic surgery suggest pulmonary embolism. Stabilize airway and breathing, escalate care, limit exertion, and prepare for urgent evaluation and treatment.

items.title: Arrange the nursing actions in the appropriate sequence for a client with heavy postpartum bleeding and a boggy uterus.
items.content: 1. Call for assistance and initiate the postpartum hemorrhage response; 2. Massage the uterine fundus and assess uterine tone; 3. Administer prescribed oxytocin and other uterotonics as indicated; 4. Establish/maintain large-bore IV access, quantify blood loss, and prepare fluids/blood products; 5. Reassess vital signs, uterine tone, and bleeding continuously.
items.rationale: A boggy uterus suggests uterine atony. Immediate help and fundal massage are followed by uterotonic therapy and simultaneous resuscitation/preparation for blood products. Continue frequent reassessment and escalate if bleeding persists.

items.title: For each electrolyte imbalance, select all manifestations that are consistent with the condition.
items.content: Hyperkalemia — peaked T waves; muscle weakness; potentially widened QRS. Hypokalemia — U waves; muscle weakness; constipation. Hyponatremia — confusion; headache; seizures when severe. Hypercalcemia — constipation; polyuria; shortened QT interval.
items.rationale: Potassium abnormalities alter cardiac conduction and muscle function. Severe hyponatremia causes cerebral edema and neurologic symptoms. Hypercalcemia commonly causes gastrointestinal slowing, polyuria, and a shortened QT interval.

items.title: A hospitalized client says, “I have been thinking about ending my life, and I know exactly how I would do it.” What should the nurse do first?
items.content: Remain with the client, initiate immediate safety precautions, and obtain urgent assessment of plan, means, and intent according to protocol.
items.rationale: A specific plan indicates high acute risk. Do not leave the client alone; secure the environment and initiate urgent safety evaluation. A promise or no-suicide contract is not a substitute for safety measures.

items.title: The nurse is teaching a client newly prescribed warfarin for atrial fibrillation. Which statements indicate correct understanding? Select all that apply.
items.content: I will have my INR checked as scheduled; I will keep my intake of vitamin K-containing foods consistent; I will contact my provider before starting OTC medicines or supplements; I will seek urgent care for black stools or uncontrolled bleeding.
items.rationale: Warfarin requires INR monitoring and consistent vitamin K intake. Many medications and supplements interact with warfarin. Melena and uncontrolled bleeding may indicate serious hemorrhage.

items.title: A 4-year-old arrives drooling, sitting upright, febrile, and leaning forward with inspiratory stridor. Select the three priority nursing actions.
items.content: Keep the child calm and in the position of comfort; summon expert airway support and prepare for controlled airway management; avoid inspecting the throat or using a tongue blade.
items.rationale: Suspected epiglottitis can progress to complete airway obstruction. Agitation and throat examination may precipitate obstruction. Maintain a calm environment and prepare for expert airway intervention.

items.title: Match each medication with the adverse effect requiring priority monitoring.
items.content: Lisinopril — angioedema; Furosemide — hypokalemia; Gentamicin — nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity; Metformin — lactic acidosis in susceptible clinical situations.
items.rationale: ACE inhibitors can cause life-threatening angioedema. Loop diuretics can lower potassium. Aminoglycosides can damage kidneys and hearing. Metformin-associated lactic acidosis is rare but serious, particularly with significant renal impairment or hypoxia.

items.title: A client with a traumatic brain injury develops a widening pulse pressure, bradycardia, and irregular respirations. This pattern is called ___ and suggests ___ intracranial pressure.
items.content: Cushing triad|increased
items.rationale: Cushing triad is a late sign of increased intracranial pressure and possible impending herniation. It requires immediate escalation and interventions to prevent further increases in ICP.

items.title: Minutes after receiving an antibiotic, a client develops generalized urticaria, wheezing, facial swelling, and BP 76/40 mm Hg. Complete the bowtie.
items.content: condition:anaphylaxis with shock|actions:administer IM epinephrine promptly per emergency protocol; support airway and oxygenation and activate emergency response|monitor:airway patency and respiratory effort; blood pressure and perfusion
items.rationale: Anaphylaxis is a life-threatening airway and circulatory emergency. IM epinephrine is first-line treatment; antihistamines are adjuncts and must not delay epinephrine. Monitor for recurrent or biphasic symptoms.

items.title: Identify the assessment findings that indicate severe features and require urgent escalation.
items.content: At 34 weeks' gestation, a client has BP 168/112 mm Hg on repeat measurement, persistent severe headache, blurred vision, and right upper-quadrant pain. Platelets are 92,000/mm³ and AST is elevated.
items.rationale: Severe-range blood pressure, neurologic symptoms, epigastric/right upper-quadrant pain, thrombocytopenia, and elevated liver enzymes indicate severe disease and risk of maternal complications, including seizure and HELLP syndrome.

items.title: A child weighs 18 kg. The prescription is amoxicillin 45 mg/kg/day divided equally every 12 hours. The suspension is 400 mg/5 mL. How many mL should be given per dose? Round to the nearest tenth.
items.content: 5.1 mL
items.rationale: Daily dose = 45 mg/kg × 18 kg = 810 mg/day. Two doses per day = 405 mg/dose. Concentration = 400 mg/5 mL = 80 mg/mL. Volume = 405 ÷ 80 = 5.06 mL, rounded to 5.1 mL. Confirm the prescription, maximum dose, and product concentration before administration.

items.title: A client admitted with dehydration has the following trend: creatinine 1.0 to 2.1 to 3.0 mg/dL over 24 hours; urine output 45 to 20 to 10 mL/hr; potassium 4.2 to 5.1 to 6.0 mEq/L. What is the priority nursing response?
items.content: Escalate immediately for worsening acute kidney injury with oliguria and dangerous hyperkalemia; obtain/maintain cardiac monitoring and prepare for prescribed hyperkalemia treatment and renal evaluation.
items.rationale: Rising creatinine, falling urine output, and potassium 6.0 mEq/L indicate worsening renal function with risk of fatal dysrhythmia. Prompt escalation, ECG monitoring, and potassium-lowering treatment are required.

items.title: A 46-year-old with a history of gallstones reports severe epigastric pain radiating to the back and repeated vomiting. Lipase is markedly elevated. HR is 118/min, BP 94/58 mm Hg, and urine output is 20 mL/hr. Which finding is the strongest indication of a developing complication requiring urgent escalation?
items.content: Hypotension with oliguria and tachycardia, indicating intravascular volume depletion and impaired organ perfusion.
items.rationale: Acute pancreatitis can cause major third spacing and systemic inflammation. Hemodynamic instability and oliguria indicate compromised perfusion and possible severe disease; prioritize resuscitation and close monitoring.

items.title: Which nursing practices reduce the risk of central line-associated bloodstream infection? Select all that apply.
items.content: Perform hand hygiene before line access; disinfect the connector for the required friction and drying time; use aseptic technique for dressing changes; assess daily whether the line remains necessary; remove the catheter promptly when no longer indicated.
items.rationale: Hand hygiene, connector disinfection, aseptic dressing care, and daily necessity review reduce contamination and line exposure. Follow the device-specific antisepsis and dressing-change protocol.

items.title: Place the nursing actions in priority order for a client with severe asthma, audible wheezing, accessory muscle use, and SpO₂ 88%.
items.content: 1. Rapidly assess airway, breathing, speech, and oxygenation while calling for urgent assistance; 2. Administer prescribed oxygen and rapid-acting inhaled bronchodilator; 3. Administer prescribed systemic corticosteroid and additional adjunct therapy as indicated; 4. Reassess work of breathing, breath sounds, oxygenation, and response; 5. Escalate immediately for exhaustion, altered mental status, or a silent chest.
items.rationale: Initial management supports oxygenation and rapidly reverses bronchospasm. Corticosteroids reduce airway inflammation but have delayed onset. A silent chest or declining consciousness signals impending respiratory failure.

items.title: For each burn-related finding, identify the appropriate nursing interpretation or response.
items.content: Hoarseness and soot around the mouth after an enclosed-space fire — suspect inhalation injury and prepare for early airway management. Circumferential chest burn with reduced chest expansion — urgent evaluation for restrictive eschar. Decreasing urine output during resuscitation — reassess perfusion and prescribed fluid titration. New confusion with hypotension — suspect inadequate perfusion and escalate.
items.rationale: Airway edema can progress rapidly after inhalation injury. Circumferential full-thickness burns may restrict ventilation or circulation. Urine output and mental status are important perfusion indicators during burn resuscitation.

items.title: A client with a chest tube for pneumothorax accidentally disconnects the drainage tubing from the collection system. What should the nurse do immediately?
items.content: Place the end of the chest tube in sterile water to re-establish a temporary water seal, then reconnect to a new drainage system per protocol.
items.rationale: A temporary sterile-water seal helps prevent air from entering the pleural space while the system is replaced. Assess respiratory status and obtain assistance; do not clamp the tube routinely because tension pneumothorax can develop.

items.title: A client experiencing acute mania is pacing, speaking rapidly, and has eaten very little. Which nursing interventions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.content: Provide a low-stimulation environment; offer high-calorie finger foods and fluids; use brief, clear directions and consistent limits; reduce competitive group activities; monitor sleep, hydration, and exhaustion.
items.rationale: Mania increases activity and distractibility while reducing attention to nutrition and rest. Low stimulation, portable nutrient-dense foods, clear limits, and monitoring support safety and basic needs.

items.title: A client with a tibial fracture in a cast reports escalating pain despite opioids. The affected foot is pale and paresthetic, and passive toe extension causes severe pain. Select the three priority actions.
items.content: Notify the orthopedic surgeon/emergency team immediately; prepare for urgent pressure-relieving intervention such as fasciotomy; perform and document frequent neurovascular assessments without delaying escalation.
items.rationale: Pain out of proportion and pain with passive stretch are early warning signs of compartment syndrome. Pulses may remain present until late. This is a limb-threatening emergency requiring immediate surgical evaluation.

items.title: Match each fetal heart rate pattern with its most likely cause.
items.content: Early decelerations — fetal head compression. Variable decelerations — umbilical cord compression. Late decelerations — uteroplacental insufficiency. Sinusoidal pattern — possible severe fetal anemia or hypoxia.
items.rationale: Early decelerations mirror contractions and are usually benign. Variable decelerations are abrupt and associated with cord compression. Late decelerations begin after the contraction starts and suggest impaired uteroplacental perfusion.

items.title: A client reports chest pressure and nausea. The ECG shows ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF. BP is 86/54 mm Hg and the client is cool and diaphoretic. Which action should the nurse take first?
items.content: Activate the emergency cardiac response and promptly assess for right ventricular involvement while supporting perfusion.
items.rationale: Inferior STEMI with hypotension may involve the right ventricle, which is preload dependent. Rapid reperfusion is essential; avoid reflexively administering nitrates when hypotension or right ventricular infarction is suspected.

items.title: A client hospitalized for heart failure is preparing for discharge. Which instructions should the nurse include? Select all that apply.
items.content: Weigh yourself every morning after urinating; report rapid weight gain according to the care plan; take medications as prescribed; follow the individualized sodium and fluid plan; report worsening dyspnea, orthopnea, or edema.
items.rationale: Daily weights can identify fluid retention before symptoms become severe. Medication adherence, individualized dietary guidance, and early reporting of congestion help prevent decompensation.

items.title: A client with cirrhosis vomits a large amount of bright-red blood and becomes pale and dizzy. BP is 78/42 mm Hg and HR is 136/min. Select the three priority nursing actions.
items.content: Activate emergency response and summon the provider; support airway and oxygenation while positioning to reduce aspiration risk; establish large-bore IV access and prepare for rapid fluid and blood-product resuscitation.
items.rationale: Hematemesis with shock indicates life-threatening hemorrhage. Airway protection, urgent escalation, and rapid vascular access/resuscitation take priority over diagnostic procedures or routine medications.

items.title: Match each arterial blood gas result with the primary acid-base disorder.
items.content: pH 7.30, PaCO₂ 55 mm Hg, HCO₃ 25 mEq/L — Uncompensated respiratory acidosis; pH 7.49, PaCO₂ 30 mm Hg, HCO₃ 24 mEq/L — Uncompensated respiratory alkalosis; pH 7.28, PaCO₂ 38 mm Hg, HCO₃ 18 mEq/L — Uncompensated metabolic acidosis; pH 7.50, PaCO₂ 42 mm Hg, HCO₃ 32 mEq/L — Uncompensated metabolic alkalosis.
items.rationale: Determine acidemia or alkalemia from pH, then identify whether PaCO₂ or bicarbonate changes in the direction explaining the pH. These examples have no meaningful compensatory change.

items.title: A client receiving chemotherapy has an absolute neutrophil count of 400/mm³ and an oral temperature of 38.3°C (100.9°F). The nurse should treat this as ___ and promptly ___ the oncology provider.
items.content: febrile neutropenia|notify
items.rationale: Fever in a severely neutropenic client is an oncologic emergency because infection may progress rapidly with few localizing signs. Prompt evaluation, cultures as ordered, and timely empiric antibiotics are critical.

items.title: A client with diabetes is found unresponsive. Capillary glucose is 32 mg/dL and IV access is present. Complete the bowtie by selecting the condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:severe hypoglycemia with impaired consciousness|actions:administer IV dextrose per protocol; protect the airway and reassess glucose after treatment|monitor:serial blood glucose; level of consciousness and airway/respiratory status
items.rationale: An unconscious client must not receive oral carbohydrate. IV dextrose is appropriate when access is available; protect the airway and repeat glucose assessment because hypoglycemia can recur.

items.title: Identify the assessment findings most consistent with acute appendicitis and possible peritoneal irritation.
items.content: A 22-year-old reports abdominal pain that began near the umbilicus and migrated to the right lower quadrant. The client has anorexia, nausea, localized guarding, and rebound tenderness. Temperature is 38.1°C.
items.rationale: Migration of pain to the right lower quadrant with localized guarding and rebound tenderness is characteristic of appendicitis with peritoneal irritation. Avoid applying heat or giving laxatives; prepare for diagnostic evaluation.

items.title: A client is prescribed 1,000 mL of normal saline over 8 hours using tubing with a drop factor of 15 gtt/mL. Calculate the manual infusion rate in drops per minute. Round to the nearest whole number.
items.content: 31 gtt/min
items.rationale: 1,000 mL × 15 gtt/mL = 15,000 drops. 8 hours × 60 minutes = 480 minutes. 15,000 ÷ 480 = 31.25, rounded to 31 gtt/min. Reassess the infusion rate and patient response per policy.

items.title: A client with septic shock has the following trend after initial fluid resuscitation: MAP 54 to 61 to 67 mm Hg; lactate 5.2 to 4.1 to 2.8 mmol/L; urine output 10 to 22 to 38 mL/hr. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
items.content: Perfusion is improving, but continued close monitoring and prescribed sepsis management are required because the client has not yet demonstrated sustained recovery.
items.rationale: Increasing MAP and urine output with falling lactate suggest improving tissue perfusion. Continue reassessment and treatment; do not discontinue monitoring solely because values are trending favorably.

items.title: A client on postpartum day 3 after cesarean birth reports chills, lower abdominal pain, and foul-smelling lochia. Temperature is 39.0°C, HR 118/min, and the uterus is tender. Which action should the nurse anticipate?
items.content: Obtain ordered cultures and promptly administer prescribed broad-spectrum IV antibiotics after cultures when this does not delay treatment.
items.rationale: Fever, uterine tenderness, and foul lochia suggest postpartum endometritis. Prompt antibiotic therapy is required; assess for sepsis and monitor hemodynamic status.

items.title: A child is admitted with fever, severe headache, neck stiffness, photophobia, and a petechial rash. Which nursing actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.content: Initiate droplet precautions promptly; notify the provider and prepare for urgent antimicrobial therapy; monitor neurologic status and signs of increased intracranial pressure; assess perfusion and signs of sepsis; use appropriate personal protective equipment during close care.
items.rationale: Suspected meningococcal disease requires immediate droplet precautions and urgent treatment. Neurologic deterioration and septic shock are major risks; do not delay antibiotics for nonessential tasks.

items.title: Arrange the key steps in the initial evaluation of a client with suspected acute stroke who may be eligible for reperfusion therapy.
items.content: 1. Activate the stroke response and determine last-known-well time; 2. Assess airway, breathing, circulation, vital signs, and bedside glucose; 3. Perform rapid neurologic assessment and establish IV access; 4. Obtain urgent noncontrast head CT to exclude hemorrhage; 5. Review eligibility, contraindications, and time window with the stroke team before treatment.
items.rationale: Stroke care is time critical. Glucose can identify a mimic, and noncontrast CT distinguishes hemorrhage from ischemia. Reperfusion decisions require rapid team review of timing and contraindications.

items.title: For each postoperative finding, select all appropriate nursing interpretations or responses.
items.content: Unilateral calf swelling and tenderness after surgery — suspect DVT and notify the provider; sudden dyspnea and pleuritic pain — suspect PE and activate emergency response; absent bowel sounds with progressive distention and vomiting — assess for ileus and notify the provider; wound evisceration — cover with sterile saline-moistened dressings and obtain immediate surgical assistance.
items.rationale: Postoperative complications require prompt recognition. Do not massage a suspected DVT. Eviscerated organs should be protected with sterile saline-moistened dressings; do not attempt to reinsert them.

items.title: A client taking digoxin reports nausea and yellow-green halos around lights. The apical pulse is 48/min. What should the nurse do?
items.content: Hold the digoxin dose and notify the provider promptly for evaluation of possible toxicity.
items.rationale: Visual disturbances, gastrointestinal symptoms, and bradycardia suggest digoxin toxicity. Withhold the dose and anticipate assessment of serum digoxin, potassium, renal function, and ECG findings.

items.title: A client with COPD has increased dyspnea, purulent sputum, and wheezing. Which interventions should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.
items.content: Administer prescribed short-acting bronchodilators; titrate oxygen to the prescribed target and reassess; administer prescribed systemic corticosteroids; obtain sputum testing or imaging as ordered; monitor for fatigue, worsening hypercapnia, and altered mental status.
items.rationale: COPD exacerbation management includes bronchodilation, controlled oxygen therapy, corticosteroids, and evaluation for infection or respiratory failure. Oxygen should be titrated to the individualized target rather than withheld.

items.title: A client with acute pancreatitis develops increasing abdominal distention, oliguria, confusion, and oxygen saturation of 88%. Select the three priority nursing responses.
items.content: Escalate urgently for possible multisystem deterioration; support oxygenation and assess respiratory status; monitor hemodynamics, urine output, and ordered laboratory trends while preparing for higher-level care.
items.rationale: Pancreatitis can cause systemic inflammatory response, third spacing, respiratory failure, and acute kidney injury. New hypoxemia, oliguria, and confusion require immediate escalation and organ-support assessment.

items.title: Match each organism or condition with the indicated precaution.
items.content: Measles — Airborne; Pertussis — Droplet; MRSA wound infection with uncontrolled drainage — Contact; Varicella — Airborne and Contact.
items.rationale: Precautions reflect transmission route. Measles and varicella require airborne isolation; varicella also requires contact precautions. Pertussis spreads by droplets, while draining MRSA wounds require contact precautions.

items.title: A client with untreated hyperthyroidism develops a temperature of 40°C, severe tachycardia, agitation, and vomiting. The nurse should suspect ___ and initiate ___ emergency response.
items.content: thyroid storm|urgent
items.rationale: Thyroid storm is a life-threatening hypermetabolic crisis. Immediate escalation, supportive care, and prescribed antithyroid, beta-blocking, and other therapies are required.

items.title: Following central venous catheter insertion, a client develops sudden severe dyspnea, absent breath sounds on the right, hypotension, and tracheal deviation. Complete the bowtie.
items.content: condition:tension pneumothorax|actions:activate emergency response and provide oxygen/ventilatory support; prepare for immediate needle or finger decompression followed by chest tube placement by a qualified clinician|monitor:oxygen saturation and respiratory effort; blood pressure and hemodynamic response
items.rationale: Unilateral absent breath sounds with shock and tracheal deviation after a procedure strongly suggests tension pneumothorax. This is an immediate life-threatening emergency requiring decompression; do not delay for imaging.

items.title: Identify the findings in this note that support suspected Kawasaki disease.
items.content: A 3-year-old has had a fever for 6 days despite antipyretics. Assessment shows bilateral nonpurulent conjunctival injection, cracked red lips, a strawberry tongue, polymorphous rash, and swollen hands and feet.
items.rationale: Prolonged fever with bilateral nonpurulent conjunctivitis, oral mucosal changes, rash, and extremity changes is characteristic of Kawasaki disease. Timely IV immunoglobulin and aspirin therapy reduce coronary artery complications.

items.title: A child weighs 24 kg. The prescribed medication dose is 10 mg/kg per dose. The available liquid contains 120 mg/5 mL. How many mL should the nurse administer per dose? Round to the nearest tenth.
items.rationale: Dose = 10 mg/kg × 24 kg = 240 mg. Concentration = 120 mg/5 mL = 24 mg/mL. Volume = 240 ÷ 24 = 10 mL. Verify the dose against the recommended range and maximum daily dose before administration.

items.title: A client admitted with melena has the following trend: HR 92 to 110 to 128/min; BP 124/76 to 106/64 to 88/52 mm Hg; hemoglobin 10.2 to 8.4 to 7.1 g/dL. What is the priority interpretation?
items.content: The client is developing hemodynamic instability from ongoing blood loss; activate urgent escalation and prepare for resuscitation and blood products as prescribed.
items.rationale: Progressive tachycardia, falling blood pressure, and declining hemoglobin indicate significant ongoing hemorrhage. Prioritize emergency assessment, vascular access, resuscitation, and definitive bleeding management.

items.title: A 74-year-old with heart failure presents with orthopnea, crackles, jugular venous distention, and bilateral edema. SpO₂ is 87%, BP 168/94 mm Hg, and chest radiograph shows pulmonary vascular congestion. Which prescribed intervention should the nurse anticipate to reduce fluid overload?
items.content: Administer IV loop diuretic therapy and monitor urine output, electrolytes, renal function, blood pressure, and respiratory response.
items.rationale: The findings indicate acute decompensated heart failure with pulmonary congestion. IV loop diuretics reduce volume overload; monitor response and electrolyte/renal complications while supporting oxygenation.

items.title: A newborn of a diabetic parent is jittery and has a bedside glucose of 34 mg/dL. Which nursing actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.content: Assess the newborn's clinical status and feeding ability; initiate the facility's neonatal hypoglycemia protocol; provide feeding or buccal dextrose gel when indicated for an appropriate asymptomatic infant; obtain repeat glucose at the protocol-specified interval; escalate promptly for symptoms or persistent low glucose and prepare for IV dextrose.
items.rationale: Newborn hypoglycemia management depends on symptoms, age, glucose level, and local protocol. Jitteriness is a symptom requiring prompt assessment and treatment; severe or persistent hypoglycemia may require IV dextrose.

items.title: Place the nursing actions in priority order when a client develops dyspnea, fever, and back pain during a blood transfusion.
items.content: 1. Stop the transfusion immediately; 2. Maintain IV access with normal saline using new tubing; 3. Assess airway, breathing, circulation, vital signs, and oxygenation and call for help; 4. Notify the provider and blood bank and follow the transfusion-reaction protocol; 5. Send the blood product and ordered specimens for investigation and document the event.
items.rationale: Stopping the blood product prevents further exposure. Maintain access with new tubing and saline, stabilize the client, and notify the appropriate teams. Follow institutional procedures for product and specimen handling.

items.title: A client with a T4 spinal cord injury develops a pounding headache, flushing above the injury, and BP 210/110 mm Hg. Select all appropriate immediate actions.
items.content: Sit the client upright; loosen restrictive clothing; check for and relieve bladder distention or catheter obstruction; assess for bowel impaction and other noxious stimuli; monitor blood pressure frequently and notify the provider urgently.
items.rationale: Autonomic dysreflexia is a hypertensive emergency in clients with injuries at or above T6. Sit upright to lower blood pressure and remove the triggering stimulus, commonly bladder distention. Do not leave the client supine.

items.title: A client with known adrenal insufficiency presents with vomiting, profound weakness, BP 74/40 mm Hg, sodium 126 mEq/L, and potassium 6.1 mEq/L. Which intervention should the nurse anticipate first?
items.content: Rapid IV isotonic fluid resuscitation and prompt IV hydrocortisone as prescribed.
items.rationale: Adrenal crisis causes life-threatening hypotension, hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia. Immediate isotonic fluids and stress-dose IV glucocorticoids are essential; monitor glucose, electrolytes, and hemodynamic response.

items.title: A 2-year-old with barking cough and stridor at rest is diagnosed with moderate-to-severe croup. Which interventions should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.
items.content: Administer prescribed dexamethasone; administer nebulized epinephrine for significant stridor at rest; keep the child calm with caregiver present; monitor respiratory effort and oxygenation after treatment; prepare for escalation if fatigue or decreasing air movement develops.
items.rationale: Corticosteroids reduce airway inflammation. Nebulized epinephrine provides temporary relief in moderate-to-severe croup and requires observation for recurrent symptoms. Agitation can worsen airway obstruction.

items.title: A client with chronic kidney disease is scheduled for a contrast-enhanced CT. Select the three nursing actions that reduce risk and support safe care.
items.content: Review current renal function and relevant history; verify the contrast plan and prescribed hydration strategy with the care team; reconcile nephrotoxic medications and follow current institutional instructions for holding or continuing them.
items.rationale: Contrast-associated kidney injury risk assessment includes baseline renal function, volume status, and medication review. Medication management should follow current orders and local guidance; do not independently discontinue essential therapies.

items.title: Match each medication or toxic exposure with the appropriate reversal agent or antidote.
items.content: Unfractionated heparin — Protamine sulfate; warfarin with life-threatening bleeding — Vitamin K plus four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate per protocol; opioid toxicity — Naloxone; acetaminophen overdose — N-acetylcysteine.
items.rationale: These agents reverse or mitigate specific toxic effects. Treatment selection and dosing depend on severity, timing, laboratory results, and current emergency protocols.

items.title: A 58-year-old reports crushing substernal pressure radiating to the jaw for 25 minutes. ECG shows ST elevation in leads II, III, and aVF. BP is 88/54 mm Hg. Which prescribed intervention should the nurse question?
items.content: Administering sublingual nitroglycerin while the client remains hypotensive.
items.rationale: Inferior STEMI with hypotension may involve right ventricular infarction and preload dependence. Nitrates can worsen hypotension; urgent reperfusion and hemodynamic support take priority.

items.title: A client is admitted after an ischemic stroke and coughs when attempting to drink water. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.content: Keep the client NPO; request a formal swallow evaluation; provide oral care; use prescribed alternative routes for medications and nutrition until swallowing is cleared.
items.rationale: Coughing with liquids indicates possible dysphagia and aspiration risk. Oral intake should be withheld pending evaluation; oral hygiene and safe alternative routes reduce complications.

items.title: A pregnant client at 34 weeks has BP 168/112 mm Hg, persistent headache, and visual spots. Select the three priority nursing actions.
items.content: Initiate seizure precautions; administer prescribed antihypertensive therapy promptly; administer magnesium sulfate as prescribed and monitor respiratory rate, reflexes, and urine output.
items.rationale: Severe-range hypertension and neurologic symptoms indicate severe features and risk for stroke and eclampsia. Treat severe blood pressure urgently and prevent seizures while monitoring for magnesium toxicity.

items.title: Match each insulin with its characteristic action profile.
items.content: Lispro — rapid acting; Regular — short acting; NPH — intermediate acting; Glargine — long acting with no pronounced peak.
items.rationale: Rapid-acting lispro is meal-associated; regular insulin is short acting; NPH has an intermediate peak; glargine provides basal coverage and should not be mixed with other insulins.

items.title: A client with kidney failure has potassium 6.8 mEq/L and peaked T waves. The nurse should anticipate IV ___ to stabilize the myocardium and insulin with dextrose to shift potassium ___ the cells.
items.content: calcium gluconate|into
items.rationale: IV calcium stabilizes cardiac membranes but does not lower serum potassium. Insulin with dextrose shifts potassium intracellularly; definitive potassium removal is also required.

items.title: Minutes after receiving an IV antibiotic, a client develops generalized urticaria, wheezing, lip swelling, and BP 76/40 mm Hg. Identify the condition, two priority actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:anaphylaxis with shock|actions:administer IM epinephrine promptly per emergency protocol; support airway and oxygenation and summon emergency response|monitor:airway patency and respiratory effort; blood pressure and perfusion
items.rationale: Anaphylaxis is a time-critical emergency. IM epinephrine is first-line; airway and circulatory support are essential. Antihistamines and corticosteroids do not replace epinephrine.

items.title: A client is 6 hours postoperative after abdominal surgery. Highlight the findings that most strongly suggest evolving hemorrhagic shock: HR 126/min; BP 86/48 mm Hg; urine output 15 mL/hr; warm dry skin; increasing restlessness; hemoglobin decreased from 12.1 to 8.2 g/dL.
items.content: segments:HR 126/min|BP 86/48 mm Hg|urine output 15 mL/hr|warm dry skin|increasing restlessness|hemoglobin decreased from 12.1 to 8.2 g/dL|correct:1,2,3,5,6
items.rationale: Tachycardia, hypotension, oliguria, restlessness, and falling hemoglobin suggest significant blood loss and impaired perfusion. Escalate immediately and prepare for resuscitation.

items.title: A prescription requires 750 mg of a medication. The reconstituted solution contains 250 mg per 5 mL. How many mL should be administered?
items.content: 15 mL
items.rationale: The concentration is 50 mg/mL. 750 mg ÷ 50 mg/mL = 15 mL. Verify the prescribed dose, concentration, and maximum dose.

items.title: A client's urine output over 4 hours is 35, 25, 18, and 12 mL/hr. Creatinine rises from 1.1 to 2.0 mg/dL. What is the priority interpretation?
items.content: Progressive oliguria with rising creatinine indicates worsening acute kidney injury; promptly notify the provider, assess volume status and perfusion, and review nephrotoxic exposures.
items.rationale: Declining urine output and rising creatinine indicate worsening renal function. Assess for reversible causes and complications such as hyperkalemia and fluid overload; do not assume fluids are appropriate without volume assessment.

items.title: A 7-year-old has fever 39.4°C, severe headache, photophobia, nuchal rigidity, and a nonblanching petechial rash. The child is lethargic. What is the priority nursing response?
items.content: Initiate droplet precautions, notify the provider and emergency team immediately, assess airway and perfusion, and prepare for prompt antimicrobial therapy and diagnostic evaluation.
items.rationale: The findings suggest bacterial meningitis, potentially meningococcal disease. Droplet precautions and urgent treatment are required; do not delay escalation for routine testing.

items.title: A client with asthma has severe dyspnea, speaks one word at a time, has minimal air movement, and SpO₂ 89%. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.content: Activate urgent response and assess airway; administer prescribed inhaled/nebulized short-acting bronchodilator; administer systemic corticosteroid as prescribed; provide oxygen and continuous reassessment; prepare for advanced airway support if fatigue or declining consciousness occurs.
items.rationale: A silent or nearly silent chest and inability to speak indicate life-threatening airflow obstruction. Rapid bronchodilation, corticosteroids, oxygen, and escalation are required.

items.title: Arrange the priority actions for a client with suspected STEMI arriving at the emergency department.
items.content: 1. Assess ABCs, obtain vital signs, and place on cardiac monitor; 2. Obtain and interpret a 12-lead ECG within the target time; 3. Establish IV access and obtain ordered blood tests without delaying reperfusion; 4. Activate the STEMI/reperfusion pathway; 5. Administer prescribed antiplatelet and other indicated therapy while preparing for urgent reperfusion.
items.rationale: Rapid ECG and activation of reperfusion are time critical. Blood tests should not delay reperfusion. Medication choices depend on contraindications and the treatment pathway.

items.title: For a client with heart failure, select all appropriate teaching points for each area.
items.content: Daily weights — weigh each morning after voiding using the same scale; worsening symptoms — report increasing dyspnea, edema, or rapid weight gain according to the action plan; medications — take prescribed therapy and do not stop diuretics independently; diet — follow individualized sodium and fluid guidance.
items.rationale: Daily weights detect fluid retention early. Symptom reporting and adherence reduce decompensation risk. Sodium and fluid limits should follow the individualized treatment plan.

items.title: A client experiencing acute mania is pacing, speaking rapidly, and unable to sit for meals. Which intervention is best?
items.content: Offer frequent high-calorie finger foods and fluids in a low-stimulation environment.
items.rationale: Clients with acute mania may be too restless to sit for meals. Portable nutrient-dense foods and reduced stimulation support nutrition and safety.

items.title: Which nursing actions reduce central-line associated bloodstream infection risk? Select all that apply.
items.content: Perform hand hygiene before line access; disinfect the needleless connector before each access; use sterile technique for dressing changes; assess daily whether the line remains necessary; replace dressings when damp, loose, or soiled.
items.rationale: Hand hygiene, hub disinfection, aseptic dressing care, and prompt removal of unnecessary lines reduce infection risk. Follow current facility policy for antiseptic and dressing intervals.

items.title: A 10-month-old has nasal flaring, intercostal retractions, grunting, and poor feeding. Select the three priority actions.
items.content: Assess airway and work of breathing immediately; provide oxygen and positioning/support appropriate to the child's condition; summon urgent pediatric support and prepare for escalation if fatigue or apnea develops.
items.rationale: Retractions, grunting, and poor feeding indicate significant respiratory distress. Rapid assessment and respiratory support are needed; infants can deteriorate quickly.

items.title: Match each arterial blood gas with the primary acid-base disorder.
items.content: pH 7.30, PaCO₂ 55, HCO₃ 24 — respiratory acidosis; pH 7.49, PaCO₂ 30, HCO₃ 23 — respiratory alkalosis; pH 7.28, PaCO₂ 38, HCO₃ 17 — metabolic acidosis; pH 7.50, PaCO₂ 47, HCO₃ 35 — metabolic alkalosis.
items.rationale: Determine whether pH is acidotic or alkalotic, then identify the PaCO₂ or bicarbonate change that explains it. These examples show primary, largely uncompensated disorders.

items.title: A pregnant client at 32 weeks reports painless, bright-red vaginal bleeding. The nurse should suspect ___ and avoid performing a ___ examination until placental location is confirmed.
items.content: placenta previa|digital vaginal
items.rationale: Painless bright-red bleeding is characteristic of placenta previa. A digital vaginal examination can disrupt the placenta and cause severe hemorrhage; ultrasound is used to locate the placenta.

items.title: A client with a urinary infection remains hypotensive after initial fluid resuscitation. MAP is 58 mm Hg, lactate 4.8 mmol/L, and extremities are cool. Complete the bowtie.
items.content: condition:septic shock with persistent tissue hypoperfusion|actions:activate sepsis escalation and administer prescribed vasopressor support; obtain cultures and administer broad-spectrum antimicrobials promptly as ordered without avoidable delay|monitor:MAP and peripheral perfusion; lactate trend and urine output
items.rationale: Persistent hypotension and elevated lactate after fluids suggest septic shock. Vasopressors are used to achieve an adequate MAP, while prompt antimicrobials and reassessment address the cause and perfusion.

items.title: A client with acute heart failure is assessed. Highlight cues requiring immediate escalation: severe dyspnea at rest; pink frothy sputum; SpO₂ 82%; new confusion; mild ankle edema unchanged for 2 weeks; crackles throughout both lungs.
items.content: segments:severe dyspnea at rest|pink frothy sputum|SpO₂ 82%|new confusion|mild ankle edema unchanged for 2 weeks|crackles throughout both lungs|correct:1,2,3,4,6
items.rationale: Severe dyspnea, frothy sputum, profound hypoxemia, confusion, and diffuse crackles suggest acute pulmonary edema and respiratory compromise. Stable chronic ankle edema is less urgent.

items.title: A client weighs 66 kg and is prescribed 0.าค5 mg/kg of a medication. The vial contains 10 mg/mL. How many mL should be administered?
items.content: 3.3 mL
items.rationale: The required dose is 0.5 mg/kg × 66 kg = 33 mg. At 10 mg/mL, the volume is 33 ÷ 10 = 3.3 mL. Confirm dose limits and rounding policy.

items.title: A client 3 days postpartum reports a severe headache and visual changes. BP readings are 148/94, 162/108, and 166/110 mm Hg over 20 minutes. What is the priority interpretation?
items.content: The client has worsening severe-range postpartum hypertension with neurologic symptoms and possible postpartum preeclampsia; arrange immediate obstetric evaluation and urgent treatment.
items.rationale: Preeclampsia can first present or worsen postpartum. Persistent severe-range blood pressure and neurologic symptoms require urgent treatment to prevent stroke and seizures.

items.title: A 76-year-old with type 2 diabetes presents with profound dehydration and confusion. Glucose is 920 mg/dL, serum osmolality 338 mOsm/kg, pH 7.36, and ketones are minimal. Which intervention is the initial priority?
items.content: Begin prescribed isotonic IV fluid replacement with frequent reassessment of hemodynamic status, sodium, potassium, glucose, and osmolality.
items.rationale: The presentation is consistent with HHS, characterized by severe hyperglycemia, hyperosmolality, and dehydration with little ketoacidosis. Fluid replacement is the initial priority; insulin and electrolyte management follow careful assessment.

items.title: A 2-hour-old newborn has an axillary temperature of 36.1°C and is jittery. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.
items.content: Initiate skin-to-skin warming or a radiant warmer as clinically appropriate; check blood glucose promptly; assess respiratory status and feeding ability; remove wet linens and use a hat and warm blankets; recheck temperature and glucose according to protocol.
items.rationale: Cold stress increases oxygen and glucose consumption. Warm the newborn, assess for hypoglycemia and respiratory compromise, and reassess response.

items.title: Place the nursing actions in priority order when an adult begins having a generalized tonic-clonic seizure in bed.
items.content: 1. Stay with the client and call for assistance; 2. Protect the head and clear nearby hazards without restraining the client; 3. Turn the client to the side when feasible and protect the airway; 4. Note seizure onset and duration and observe characteristics; 5. After movements stop, assess airway, breathing, neurologic status, and recovery.
items.rationale: Safety and airway protection are priorities. Never restrain the client or place objects in the mouth. Timing and postictal assessment guide subsequent treatment.

items.title: For each medication situation, select all appropriate nursing checks or actions.
items.content: Digoxin — assess apical pulse and follow hold parameters; opioid analgesic — assess sedation and respiratory status; potassium chloride IV — dilute and administer using an infusion pump, never IV push; insulin — verify dose, type, timing, and glucose with required safeguards.
items.rationale: These medications have significant risks: bradycardia with digoxin, respiratory depression with opioids, fatal dysrhythmia with rapid potassium administration, and hypoglycemia or wrong-insulin errors.

items.title: A client's chest tube becomes disconnected from the drainage system, but the tube remains in the chest. What should the nurse do immediately?
items.content: Place the end of the chest tube in sterile water to re-establish a temporary water seal and obtain a new drainage system.
items.rationale: If the tube disconnects from the drainage unit, placing its end in sterile water creates a temporary water seal while a new system is obtained. Follow facility emergency procedure and reassess respiratory status.

items.title: A client with cirrhosis is confused and has asterixis. Which interventions should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.
items.content: Administer prescribed lactulose and monitor stool response; assess for infection, GI bleeding, constipation, and medication triggers; monitor mental status and airway protection; trend electrolytes and renal function; implement fall and injury precautions.
items.rationale: Hepatic encephalopathy is often precipitated by infection, bleeding, constipation, dehydration, or sedating medications. Lactulose reduces ammonia absorption; monitor response and safety.

items.title: A client with a forearm fracture in a cast reports escalating pain, pain with passive finger extension, and new paresthesia. Select the three priority actions.
items.content: Notify the orthopedic provider immediately; perform and document focused neurovascular assessment; prepare for urgent cast release or fasciotomy as prescribed.
items.rationale: Pain out of proportion, passive-stretch pain, and paresthesia suggest compartment syndrome. Prompt decompression may be required to prevent irreversible tissue injury.

items.title: Match each finding with the likely congenital heart condition.
items.content: Cyanosis that improves with squatting — Tetralogy of Fallot; continuous machinery-like murmur — Patent ductus arteriosus; fixed split S2 — Atrial septal defect; bounding pulses and widened pulse pressure — Patent ductus arteriosus.
items.rationale: Tetralogy spells may improve with knee-chest positioning or squatting. PDA produces continuous flow and bounding pulses; ASD is associated with a fixed split second heart sound.

items.title: A client with myasthenia gravis develops weak cough, difficulty swallowing, and declining vital capacity. The nurse should prioritize assessment of ___ and prepare for possible ___.
items.content: respiratory function|intubation and mechanical ventilation
items.rationale: Bulbar weakness and declining vital capacity indicate impending respiratory failure. Airway and ventilation assessment and early escalation are essential; avoid delaying support until arrest.

items.title: A client with hematemesis becomes pale and diaphoretic. HR is 138/min, BP 78/42 mm Hg, and hemoglobin 6.9 g/dL. Identify the condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:hemorrhagic shock from acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding|actions:activate emergency response and establish large-bore IV access for prescribed resuscitation; prepare for blood products and urgent endoscopic management|monitor:hemodynamic status and mental status; urine output and hemoglobin trend
items.rationale: Tachycardia, hypotension, pallor, and severe anemia indicate hemorrhagic shock. Resuscitation and definitive bleeding control are urgent; monitor perfusion and response.

items.title: A client receiving chemotherapy has an ANC of 300/mm³ and temperature 38.4°C. Highlight findings or actions requiring immediate attention: new chills; hypotension 90/54 mm Hg; avoid rectal temperatures; obtain ordered blood cultures promptly; delay antibiotics until the next routine medication round; new confusion.
items.content: segments:new chills|hypotension 90/54 mm Hg|avoid rectal temperatures|obtain ordered blood cultures promptly|delay antibiotics until the next routine medication round|new confusion|correct:1,2,3,4,6
items.rationale: Fever with profound neutropenia is an oncologic emergency. Chills, hypotension, and confusion may indicate sepsis. Obtain cultures promptly if this does not delay broad-spectrum antibiotics; avoid rectal procedures because of mucosal injury risk.

items.title: A child is prescribed 480 mL of IV fluid over 6 hours. What rate should the nurse program in mL/hr?
items.content: 80 mL/hr
items.rationale: 480 mL ÷ 6 hr = 80 mL/hr. Verify the prescribed volume and rate against the child's weight-based fluid plan and pump settings.
